# Tern of Remote Monitoring (`tern-of-remote-monitoring`)

Checks remote patient monitoring billing: device supply codes against days of readings in each 30-day period, overlapping periods, setup billed more than once per episode, management minutes and add-on units, months with no interactive contact, and RPM billed with remote therapeutic monitoring. Patient names are masked before results reach the model.

**Tern never submits or changes claims. Tern never reads, interprets or acts on the readings.**

Kestrel ver 1 · Care management and value-based care · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`kestrel-core`](../kestrel-core)

```bash
npx -y tern-of-remote-monitoring demo
npx -y tern-of-remote-monitoring mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: a made-up cardiology practice's monitoring program, made-up patients. Any likeness to real people is chance.

- [`readings.csv`](fixtures/readings.csv), [`management-time.csv`](fixtures/management-time.csv), [`claims.csv`](fixtures/claims.csv) and [`enrolled.csv`](fixtures/enrolled.csv), mostly October 2026. Planted:
  - T1: 99454 for October with 12 days of readings (16 needed; 99445 fits).
  - T2: setup 99453 billed in August and again in October in the same episode.
  - T3: 99457 for October with 25 minutes but no interactive contact logged.
  - T4: 45 minutes with 99457 and two units of 99458 (the time supports one).
  - T5: 99454 for the period ending October 15 and again for the period ending October 31; they overlap.
  - T6: RPM and remote therapeutic monitoring (98980) billed in the same month.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): example rates. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `tern_check` | List repeat setups, overlapping periods, short reading days, RTM overlaps, months with no interactive contact and short minutes. | runs |
| `tern_write_report` | Write tern-remote-monitoring.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and tern-remote-monitoring.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/tern). | runs |
| `tern_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `tern_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `tern_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `tern_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `claim_submit` | Tern never submits or changes claims. | refused |
| `reading_interpret` | Tern never reads, interprets or acts on the readings. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `tern_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `readings` (required) | Device readings under --root: patient and reading date (one row per reading or per day) |
| `time` (required) | Management time log: patient, date, minutes, interactive contact (yes/no) |
| `claims` (required) | Monitoring claim lines: patient, date of service, code, units, period start |
| `patients` | Optional enrolled patients: patient, episode start |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: rates |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx tern-of-remote-monitoring inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Readings (`readings`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `date` (required) | date | Reading Date, Date, Measured, Timestamp, Reading Time, Transmission Date |

### Management time (`time`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `date` (required) | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `minutes` (required) | number | Minutes, Min, Mins, Duration, Duration (min), Time (min), Total Minutes, Treatment Minutes |
| `interactive` | text | Interactive, Interactive Contact, Live Contact, Two-way, Call Completed |

### Claims (`claims`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `date` (required) | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `cpt` (required) | text | CPT, Code, Procedure, Procedure Code, CPT/HCPCS, HCPCS, Service Code, Proc Code |
| `units` | number | Units, Unit, Qty, Quantity, Days/Units, Service Units |
| `period_start` | date | Period Start, From, From Date, Start |

### Enrolled patients (`patients`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` (required) | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `episode_start` | date | Episode Start, Enrolled, Enrollment Date, Start Date, Program Start |

## Settings file (`tern_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `rates` | Expected payment by code, for dollar estimates |

## Memory

`tern_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `tern_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `kestrel-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tern-of-remote-monitoring": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "tern-of-remote-monitoring",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add tern-of-remote-monitoring -- npx -y tern-of-remote-monitoring mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
tern-of-remote-monitoring tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
tern-of-remote-monitoring sources               # the columns each input is read from
tern-of-remote-monitoring inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
tern-of-remote-monitoring call tern_check '{"readings":"<readings>","time":"<time>","claims":"<claims>"}'
tern-of-remote-monitoring eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
tern-of-remote-monitoring demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
